links.speaker: Lakshmi
links.quote: Um, yes. I think we should do the summit again. In person, at the Harborview Hotel, in the ballroom.

links.speaker: Greta
links.quote: Late November. Okay, so, we're booking the Harborview ballroom for the summit.

links.speaker: Greta
links.quote: Yes, do that. Newsletter goes out the fifteenth, so draft by the tenth.

links.speaker: Lakshmi
links.quote: The summits have generated more pipeline than anything else we've tried, and customers tell us in the survey that they love meeting the product team face to face.

links.speaker: Greta
links.quote: I got an email from the Harborview yesterday. They're closing the ballroom for renovation through the end of the year. And I called around, and the next best venue wants a deposit that's eighteen thousand over what we budgeted.

links.speaker: Greta
links.quote: So, with the venue closing and the cost, we can't keep the summit plan as it was. I want to open it back up.

links.speaker: Noor
links.quote: Big picture, we want to keep customers close and still drive pipeline. What about a virtual product showcase? With a small invite-only reception for the top accounts, in our own office. It costs way less than a hotel, we reach customers who can't travel, and the reception keeps that personal touch for the accounts that matter most.

links.speaker: Greta
links.quote: Okay. Then I'm deciding: we're switching to a virtual product showcase plus a small invite-only reception.

links.speaker: Noor
links.quote: I looked at three. The one I like is four dollars an attendee and handles registration and reminders automatically.

links.speaker: Greta
links.quote: Sign up for it. Lakshmi, the reception, we need a guest list.

links.speaker: Greta
links.quote: Send it to me. And put the start date in.
